report_markdown:
## Question

What is the oscillation period of this spring pendulum: a small metal weight on a hanging coil spring swinging side-to-side?

## What Physicam saw

Physicam tracked the metal weight, described as a small shiny metal bob at the bottom of the spring, in track t1. The track contains 491 frames from 0.433 s to 16.767 s. The video has 504 frames, a duration of 16.800 s, a frame rate of 30.00 fps, and dimensions of $720 \times 1280$ px. Motion blur was noted. The camera was static, and the motion analysed was the bob's lateral position, $x(t)$.

## Method

No spatial calibration was available or needed for a period measurement: the calibration method was “none.” Three fits were compared over the tracked interval. A pendulum fit (f0) was attempted over 0.433–16.767 s. Because its circle-fit pivot was not above the bob and its fit quality was poor, the period was instead taken from a damped-sinusoid oscillator fit (f1) to $x(t)$ over the same interval, following the reported answer. A second oscillator fit (f2) over 0.433–8.500 s, using 243 points, provided a consistency check. Period stability was also assessed using the two half-range periods from f1.

## Results

| Fit | Range (s) | Points | Period (s) | $R^2$ | RMSE (px) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Pendulum f0 | 0.433–16.767 | 491 | $0.9648 \pm 0.0058$ | 0.6896 | 221.9 |
| Oscillator f1 | 0.433–16.767 | 491 | $0.9633 \pm 0.0039$ | 0.9653 | 22.81 |
| Oscillator f2 | 0.433–8.500 | 243 | $0.9603 \pm 0.0078$ | 0.9685 | 23.92 |

The adopted result is $T = 0.963 \pm 0.006$ s. For f1, $\omega = 6.522 \pm 0.026$ rad/s, $\gamma = 0.024 \pm 0.015$ s$^{-1}$, amplitude $= 204 \pm 25$ px, and $k/m = 42.54 \pm 0.34$ s$^{-2}$. Its half-range periods were 0.961 s and 0.967 s.

## Discussion

No accepted period is provided, so no direct comparison with an accepted value is possible. The pendulum fit's length implied by assuming $g = 9.81$ m/s$^2$, $0.076 \pm 0.025$ m, is a derived fact rather than a measurement of $g$; $g$ itself was not computed because there was no calibrated length.

The oscillator fits agree: f1 and f2 periods differ by less than their uncertainties, and f1's half-range periods are close. This supports a stable period near 0.963 s. Nevertheless, residuals indicate substantial unmodelled structure. For f1, $\chi^2_{\rm red} = 63.99$, with a warning of “large residual structure: maybe air drag, perspective, or wrong model”; f2 similarly has $\chi^2_{\rm red} = 94.38$. The pendulum fit was much worse, with $R^2 = 0.6896$, RMSE $= 221.9$ px, and an invalid pivot geometry. For f1, the systematic period component, 0.0032 s, exceeded the statistical component, 0.0022 s; period was also listed as the dominant error for f0. Motion blur likely contributed to tracking residuals.

## How to measure better next time

Reduce motion blur with brighter illumination or a shorter exposure, keep the swing in a plane parallel to the image to limit perspective effects, and record a calibrated length scale in view. That would permit a genuine pendulum-length and $g$ analysis rather than relying only on $x(t)$. A longer, less-blurred track with repeated swings would also help separate damping, drag, and model mismatch in the residuals.
